source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: When choosing a material for an object, decide whether the material's properties fit the object's purpose.
node_labels: Matter: materials, particles, mixtures and change

mx.teacher_note: This plastic container is suitable for cooking because it holds water, even though it melts when heated.

mx.teacher_note: Choose the blue cloth for the tumbler because blue is the colour of water, even though it leaks.

intelligence.enrichment: A material is chosen for making an object depending on its properties and the purpose for which the object is to be used. Different parts of one object may use different materials when their purposes differ. purpose of the object plus material properties -> suitable or unsuitable material choice The learner correctly applies this rule: A material is chosen for making an object depending on its properties and the purpose for which the object is to be used. Different parts of one object may use different materials when their purposes differ. A material chosen for an object automatically works for that purpose, so a cloth tumbler should hold water if called a tumbler.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Materials around us. The student must decide: When choosing a material for an object, decide whether the material's properties fit the object's purpose. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
